## How to use this list

- 🧭 Organized **Region → Park or City → State → Activity → Trail or Site** — e.g. Southwest → Zion National Park → Utah → Sunrise → Canyon Overlook. Counts: Northeast 81 · Southeast 169 · Midwest 99 · Southwest 162 · Mountain West 94 · West 125 · Pacific Northwest 61 · Alaska 37 · Hawaii 8 · U.S. Territories 3 · **Total 839**
- 📍 Every place name links to its Google Maps location. Each entry also shows what the reel recommended it for and links to that reel.
- 🎬 **Source reel** links go back to the original Instagram reel, so you can re-watch why it was saved — tap the **🎬 Sources** dropdown under any place to see them.
- 💬 **Ask the chatbot** — tap the **Ask Bot** button at the bottom-left of this page (and the map) to chat right here, or open [Reel Chat](chat.html) full-screen. It is the project's one chatbot (the Streamlit app): it answers questions and builds itineraries from these recommendations.

### Acadia National Park

##### Beach

- **1. [Sand Beach](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Sand Beach, Acadia National Park, Bar Harbor, Maine)** — Acadia National Park, Bar Harbor
  - **Best for:** Beach / First of the notable stops on their Acadia coastal list — Named first among the 'notable stops along the coast of Acadia National Park' in their moody, foggy-day post: Sand Beach — the park's only sandy ocean beach, about 290 yards long in Newport Cove on the Park Loop Road.
  - Coordinates: NPS Acadia GPS chart (Sand Beach parking area).

##### Hike

- **2. [Penobscot Mountain Trail](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Penobscot+Mountain+Trail+Acadia+National+Park+ME)** — Acadia National Park, Bar Harbor
  - **Best for:** Hike — Acadia's hidden gem, just across Jordan Pond from the busy Bubbles hikes — a 2.9-mile out-and-back with 980 feet of gain, starting along the Jordan Pond shoreline and climbing exposed granite ledges to a roughly 1,200-foot summit with 360-degree views of the pond, the surrounding mountains and the Atlantic coastline. Rated hard on AllTrails; a quieter side of the park away from the busier trails.
  - 🥾 AllTrails: [Trail page](https://www.alltrails.com/trail/us/maine/penobscot-mountain-trail)
  - Coordinates: Penobscot Mountain summit, USGS GNIS via TopoQuest 44.332851,-68.26668 (elev. 1,194 ft); Mapcarta 44.33286,-68.26668 agrees. Trail feature itself at 44.32758,-68.26446.
  <details><summary>🎬 Sources</summary>
  <ul>
  <li><a href="https://www.instagram.com/reel/DfniyeIICMI/">Experience one of Acadia&#x27;s hidden gems!</a> by @ryan.goes.hiking</li>

  </details>
- **3. [Precipice Trail](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Precipice+Trail+Acadia+National+Park+ME)** — Acadia National Park, Acadia National Park
  - **Best for:** Hike / Adrenaline — His #1 adrenaline hike: climbers ascending near-vertical granite using iron rungs and ladders, with coastal ocean views from the summit. Across the countdown he frames the five as thrilling but accessible adventures, describing each hike's challenge, exposure and reward.
  - 🥾 AllTrails: [Trail page](https://www.alltrails.com/trail/us/maine/precipice-loop)
  - Pin is the trailhead point on the Park Loop Road (OSM's 'The Precipice Trail' information point).

### Acadia National Park (Sieur de Monts)

#### Maine

##### Hike · Short historic stone-step path to Dorr Mountain

- **15. [Homans Path](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Homans+Path+Acadia)** — Acadia National Park (Sieur de Monts), Bar Harbor
  - **Best for:** Hike · Short historic stone-step path to Dorr Mountain — One of the shortest hikes in Acadia National Park might also be one of the most unique: tucked into the Sieur de Monts area near Bar Harbor, Homans Path is just 0.3 miles one way (0.8 mi out-and-back with ~334 ft of climb) but packs in intricate granite staircases, narrow forest passages, historic stonework, a stone 'hallway' and beautiful views on a short but steep climb. The reel pairs it into a half-day Sieur de Monts itinerary: Wild Gardens of Acadia, the Nature Center, the Jesup Path boardwalk, then Homans Path, with the Island Explorer shuttle as an option. The path is a memorial trail honoring Eliza Lothrop Homans' land donations; it joins the Schiff Path toward the summit of Dorr Mountain.
  - 🥾 AllTrails: [Trail page](https://www.alltrails.com/trail/us/maine/homans-path--2)
  - Pin is Sieur de Monts Spring — the trail begins at Sieur de Monts, steps from the spring and the Wild Gardens of Acadia.
  <details><summary>🎬 Sources</summary>
  <ul>
  <li><a href="https://www.instagram.com/reel/Dd0ePLKxuJF/">One of the shortest hikes in Acadia might be the most unique: Homans Path</a> by @the_roamsteaders</li>
  </ul>
  </details>

### Monadnock State Park

#### New Hampshire

##### Hike

- **56. [Mount Monadnock](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Mount+Monadnock+New+Hampshire)** — Monadnock State Park, Jaffrey
  - **Best for:** Hike / Summit · Bare rocky summit with 360° views — Calvin's reel takes on Mt. Monadnock in southern New Hampshire — the 3,165-ft peak that gave 'monadnock' its name (an isolated mountain rising from the plain), reputed to be one of the most-climbed mountains in the world. The classic route is the White Dot Trail up from the state park headquarters (3.4–3.6 mi round trip, ~1,750 ft gain, with rock scrambles and stone steps) and down the White Cross — the bare, rocky summit opens to sweeping views across southern New Hampshire and, on clear days, all six New England states. A National Natural Landmark with a literary streak: Emerson and Thoreau both climbed and wrote about it. No dogs allowed on the mountain.
  - 🥾 AllTrails: [Trail page](https://www.alltrails.com/trail/us/new-hampshire/white-dot-to-mount-monadnock)

### Buffalo National River (Ponca Wilderness)

#### Arkansas

##### Hike · Narrow ledge trail on a 550-ft bluff over the Buffalo River

- **32. [Goat Trail to Big Bluff](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Centerpoint+Trailhead+Ponca+Arkansas)** — Buffalo National River (Ponca Wilderness), Ponca
  - **Best for:** Hike · Narrow ledge trail on a 550-ft bluff over the Buffalo River — A strenuous 6-mile round trip in the Ponca Wilderness: follow the Centerpoint Trail down from Highway 43, then take the Goat Trail spur — a narrow ledge carved across the face of Big Bluff, at 550 feet one of the tallest sheer bluffs between the Rockies and the Appalachians — for the huge view over the Buffalo River. Rugged, rocky, and a real climb back out; the reel's trail warning is plenty of horse poop along the way. Not for kids or anyone afraid of heights.
  - 🥾 AllTrails: [Trail page](https://www.alltrails.com/trail/us/arkansas/goat-trail-to-big-bluff)
  - Pin is the Centerpoint Trailhead on AR-43 north of Ponca (the hike's start); Big Bluff is about 3 trail-miles in.
  <details><summary>🎬 Sources</summary>
  <ul>
  <li><a href="https://www.instagram.com/reel/DfM53guRj7X/">You hiked 6 miles to see THIS Arkansas view</a> by @heyarkansas</li>
  </ul>
  </details>

##### Waterfall

- **33. [Hemmed-In Hollow Falls](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Hemmed-in-Hollow+Falls+Arkansas)** — Buffalo National River (Ponca Wilderness), Compton
  - **Best for:** Waterfall / Hike · Tallest waterfall between the Rockies and Appalachians — A nearly 210-foot waterfall hidden in the Ponca Wilderness of Buffalo National River — the tallest waterfall between the Rocky and Appalachian Mountains. The journey is part of it: a steep, rugged hike drops nearly 1,400 feet into the hollow, and you climb every bit of it back out. Key catch from the reel: it's rain-fed, so it can be a powerful cascade after significant rainfall or barely a trickle in dry periods — go after rain (late winter through spring is peak flow).
  - 🥾 AllTrails: [Trail page](https://www.alltrails.com/trail/us/arkansas/hemmed-in-hollow-trail)
  <details><summary>🎬 Sources</summary>

### Channels State Forest

#### Virginia

##### Hike

- **47. [The Great Channels](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=The Great Channels, Channels State Forest, Saltville, Virginia)** — Channels State Forest, Saltville
  - **Best for:** Hike / Sandstone slot-canyon maze atop Middle Knob — Southwest Virginia's awe-inspiring labyrinth of 400-million-year-old sandstone: a 6.4-mile moderate hike (they clocked 6.9 with maze detours) climbing about 1,300 feet to the crevice maze atop Middle Knob.   - Coordinates: published Waymarking point for the Channels formation beside the Middle Knob fire tower (N 36°52.260 W 081°58.789). Trailhead parking is at Hayter's Gap on VA-80.

### Devil's Den Spring (private)

#### Florida

##### Swimming

- **61. [Devil's Den Prehistoric Spring](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Devil's+Den+Spring+Williston+Florida)** — Devil's Den Spring (private), Williston
  - **Best for:** Swimming / Snorkel & dive · Underground spring inside a dry cave — Episode 1 of Jete's American Bucket List: Devil's Den in Williston, Florida (5390 NE 180th Ave) — you can swim inside the earth. It's an underground spring in a dry cave, over 100 feet across, reached only by descending a staircase into the sinkhole; it got its name because people once saw 'smoke' (winter steam) rising from the hole and thought it was where the devil lives. The water is 72°F year-round and you can snorkel or scuba dive — the reel's headline price was $30. Animal fossils from millions of years ago (Pleistocene finds, now at the UF Museum of Natural History) have been found down there.
  - Coordinates are the published Devil's Den Cave point (Wikipedia); the business's own listing puts it at the same spot (±0.001°). The Dyrt's printed coordinates (29.439, -82.530) are wrong and were rejected.
  <details><summary>🎬 Sources</summary>

### Devil's Fork Loop Trail / Jefferson National Forest

#### Virginia

##### Swimming hole

- **62. [Devil's Bathtub](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Devil's+Bathtub+Virginia)** — Devil's Fork Loop Trail / Jefferson National Forest, Fort Blackmore
  - **Best for:** Swimming hole / Hike · Emerald rock pool down 13 creek crossings — 13 creek crossings to reach a bathtub the creek carved for itself: Devil's Bathtub near Fort Blackmore, VA (Scott County, ~30 min from Natural Tunnel) — emerald water swirling through a smooth rock pool, and the name is backed by ~65°F water even in July. The reel's practical card: the Devil's Fork Trail is ~4 mi round trip with 13 unbridged crossings (or a 7-mi no-crossing route), budget 3–5 hours and 3 PM as the last start; don't go if the water is above your knees — the holler flash floods; free lot at 312 High Knob SC, Dungannon VA (no roadside parking — towed); go weekdays or early. Swimming season is over by fall — the hike is the experience then.
  - Pin is the OSM attraction point for Devil's Bathtub itself.

### Jefferson National Forest

#### Virginia

##### Waterfall

- **96. [Cascades Falls](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Cascades+Falls+Pembroke+VA)** — Jefferson National Forest, Pembroke
  - **Best for:** Waterfall / 66-foot waterfall at the end of a creekside climb — One of the best hikes in Virginia, and the waterfall is incredible: Cascades Falls in Pembroke, Virginia — she hiked it with her 8-year-old. It's 2 miles out and 2 miles back plus lots of elevation gain — a hard hike for beginners, but doable with kids (not recommended for kids under 6). About 4 hours from northern Virginia and 3 hours from Richmond. Her tips for solo moms and solo adventurers: bring way more water than you think you'll need and be prepared to take many breaks. (The falls themselves are a 66-foot cascade on Little Stony Creek, reached by the Cascades National Recreation Trail — US Forest Service.)
  - 🥾 AllTrails: [Trail page](https://www.alltrails.com/trail/us/virginia/cascades-falls-trail)
  - Pin is the falls themselves on Little Stony Creek (published waterfall GPS; trail guides and the Forest Service agree). The Cascades Day Use Area trailhead/parking is ~1.5 mi southwest at 37.35301, -80.59984 (2068 Cascade Dr, $3/car day-use fee).

### Parthenon

#### Arkansas

##### Stay

- **125. [Beckham Creek Cave Lodge](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Beckham+Creek+Cave+Lodge+Parthenon+AR)** — Parthenon, Parthenon
  - **Best for:** Stay / Unique stay · Sleep inside a living cave in the Ozarks — Would you stay the night in this cave? Buried in the Ozark Mountains, Beckham Creek Cave Lodge (@beckhamcave) in Parthenon, Arkansas was once a private Cold War fallout shelter and has since been converted into one of the most beautiful and unique homes in the world. The 5,800 sq ft cave has 4 bedrooms, each with its own bathroom, and comfortably sleeps up to 12 guests — for less than $300 a person per night with a group. It was featured on Netflix's “World's Most Amazing Vacation Rentals,” and they offer cave tours you can take without staying the night.
  - Pin is the lodge's published point (1110 NC 8641, Parthenon, AR 72666) — the business listing, the Newton County Chamber's map embed, and showcaves.com all agree within ~150 ft.
  <details><summary>🎬 Sources</summary>

### Rainbow Springs State Park

#### Florida

##### Spring swimming · Kayak a crystal-clear 72°F river

- **130. [Rainbow Springs State Park](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Rainbow+Springs+State+Park+FL)** — Rainbow Springs State Park, Dunnellon
  - **Best for:** Spring swimming · Kayak a crystal-clear 72°F river — One of the oldest and most beautiful spring-fed rivers in Florida: crystal-clear water at 72°F year-round, surrounded by lush greenery that feels like a tropical jungle. It's Florida's 4th-largest spring; the headspring area was a privately owned theme park in the 1930s. Kayak, paddleboard, swim in the designated area, or walk the garden trails to see waterfalls — real ones, in Florida. Open daily 8 AM to sunset, $2 entry (tubing and kayak rentals extra). Pro tip from the reel: come early morning or late afternoon to beat the crowds, and bring your own snorkel gear to spot fish and turtles.
  <details><summary>🎬 Sources</summary>

##### Hike

- **137. [Bearfence Mountain Trail](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Bearfence+Mountain+Trail+Shenandoah+National+Park+VA)** — Shenandoah National Park, Shenandoah National Park
  - **Best for:** Hike / Short rock-scramble summit with a 360-degree view — From Kelley & Carl's Virginia fall itinerary: a moderate 1.1-mile hike with some rock scrambling. Their fall-hikes list: 1.1 miles round trip, 239 ft of gain — and breathtaking at sunrise, which is also their Shenandoah photography pick.
  - 🥾 AllTrails: [Trail page](https://www.alltrails.com/trail/us/virginia/bearfence-mountain-trail)
  - Pin is the OSM Bearfence Mountain summit point.

  - **Best for:** Hike / Easy walk to a boulder-field summit in Shenandoah's South District — From Kelley & Carl's Virginia fall itinerary: an easy 1.2-mile hike to Blackrock Summit — a short Appalachian Trail walk to a sea of quartzite boulders with wide views.

- **140. [Stony Man](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Stony+Man+Shenandoah+National+Park+VA)** — Shenandoah National Park, Shenandoah National Park
  - **Best for:** Hike / Shenandoah's second-highest summit, big Shenandoah Valley views — From Kelley & Carl's Virginia fall itinerary: a moderate 1.5-mile hike to Stony Man's summit. Their fall-hikes list adds the numbers — 1.5-mile loop, 318 ft of gain, panoramic views over the Shenandoah Valley. Also a Day 1-3 hike on their East Coast fall road trip.
  - 🥾 AllTrails: [Trail page](https://www.alltrails.com/trail/us/virginia/stony-man-via-appalachian-trail)

##### Hiking

- **142. [Mary's Rock](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Mary's Rock, Shenandoah National Park, Shenandoah National Park, Virginia)** — Shenandoah National Park, Shenandoah National Park
  - **Best for:** Hiking / Summit viewpoint via the Appalachian Trail — One of their favorite Shenandoah hikes: the 3,514-foot summit just south of Thornton Gap, a short steep Appalachian Trail climb to a wide panorama.
  - 🥾 AllTrails: [Trail page](https://www.alltrails.com/trail/us/virginia/marys-rock-via-appalachian-trail-north-approach)

### Apostle Islands National Lakeshore

#### Wisconsin

##### Ice caves

- **3. [Apostle Islands Ice Caves](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Apostle Islands Ice Caves, Apostle Islands National Lakeshore, Bayfield, Wisconsin)** — Apostle Islands National Lakeshore, Bayfield
  - **Best for:** Ice caves / Walk to frozen sea caves when Lake Superior freezes — #2 on her winter bucket list: plan a trip around the Apostle Islands ice caves. In summer the mainland sea caves are a kayak trip — she shows a kayak POV under massive icicles and warns it takes advanced skills — but when the lake freezes, the National Park Service opens foot access across the ice; some winters the window lasts only a day.
  - Coordinates: NPS-published Meyers Beach trailhead GPS (go.nps.gov/IceCaves); the caves form along the mainland cliffs east of the trailhead. NPS opens ice-cave access only when ice conditions are safe — 2015, then briefly again in February 2026.

### Artist Point

##### Sunrise

- **4. [Artist Point](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Artist Point, Artist Point, Grand Marais, Minnesota)** — Artist Point, Grand Marais
  - **Best for:** Sunrise / Sub-zero sunrise over frozen Lake Superior — #1 on her Lake Superior winter bucket list: watching sunrise at Artist Point in Grand Marais, Minnesota, over the frozen lake when it is 20 degrees below zero or colder. The rocky point is minutes from a parking lot; her advice is to dress warm, stay back from the water's edge, and wear microspikes.

### Beverly Shores (Indiana Dunes)

#### Indiana

##### Stargazing · Night sky over Lake Michigan by the dunes

- **20. [Beverly Shores](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Beverly+Shores+Indiana)** — Beverly Shores (Indiana Dunes), Beverly Shores
  - **Best for:** Stargazing · Night sky over Lake Michigan by the dunes — From Midwest Living's '20 Midwest Escapes for Epic Stargazing' — a pick for taking advantage of the longer nights to stargaze, learn astronomy, or spot the northern lights. Featured at dusk with the Chicago skyline across the lake — the Indiana Dunes town is an International Dark Sky Community, so the stars come out once the sun drops.

### Custer State Park (Needles Highway)

#### South Dakota

##### Scenic drive · One-lane tunnel carved through granite

- **34. [Needles Eye Tunnel](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Needles+Eye+Tunnel+South+Dakota)** — Custer State Park (Needles Highway), Custer
  - **Best for:** Scenic drive · One-lane tunnel carved through granite — The Needles Highway through Custer State Park winds between towering granite spires until the road tightens and passes through the Needles Eye Tunnel — a one-lane tunnel hand-carved through solid granite in the 1920s, one of the most photographed drives in the Black Hills. Know before you go: the tunnel is about 8'4" wide and 12' tall, one vehicle at a time, and RVs/trailers should avoid the route; drive it early morning or late afternoon for fewer cars and better light, and watch for bison, pronghorn and prairie dogs nearby.

- **72. [Pinnacles Youth Park](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Pinnacles+Youth+Park+Missouri)** — Pinnacles Youth Park, Sturgeon
  - **Best for:** Hike · Towering rock pinnacles and fossil hunting — One of the most unique places in Missouri: a privately owned park north of Columbia (850 E. Pinnacles Rd, Sturgeon) that's open for public day use and feels like a rugged hike out west. Lower trails run along the creek to a shelter bluff for all ages; the real adventure is crossing the creek and taking the narrow, rocky path over the top of the towering rock formations. The spot is full of fossils — look in the creek and across the rocks for thousands of crinoids. Free (donation box at the kiosk); vault restroom; no alcohol, glass or drones. The reel's warnings: the upper ledge trails are not for young kids or anyone afraid of heights, don't cross the creek when the water is high, and expect wet feet even in summer.
  <details><summary>🎬 Sources</summary>
  <ul>
  <li><a href="https://www.instagram.com/reel/DfYsfYBOaqy/">This is Missouri?! Pinnacles Youth Park</a> by @midwestnomadfamily</li>

### Polish Triangle (Polonia Triangle)

#### Illinois

##### Landmark

- **73. [Chicago Self-Cleaning Public Toilet](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Polonia+Triangle+Chicago+IL)** — Polish Triangle (Polonia Triangle), Chicago
  - **Best for:** Landmark / Chicago's first self-cleaning public toilet — Chicago's first standalone automated public restroom — a JCDecaux kiosk in the Polish Triangle at Milwaukee, Ashland and Division, above the Division Blue Line station, which opened with a ceremonial 'First Flush' on the day this reel was posted (installation had wrapped Oct 23). Kwon tours it: free to use, spacious and ADA-compliant, with a 15-minute limit, an exit button plus a low foot-tap emergency button, and a combined sink/hand-dryer. After each use the toilet retracts into a side compartment where high-pressure jets wash and disinfect it (about a 30-second cycle), so the seat and paper can be slightly moist — she still calls it probably the nicest public bathroom she has ever used.
  - Coordinates: Wikipedia's Polonia Triangle plaza point (41.903579,-87.667176), matching the Polish Triangle Coalition place record for 1204 N Milwaukee Ave; the kiosk stands in the plaza (Fox 32 Chicago / Block Club Chicago).
  <details><summary>🎬 Sources</summary>

  <li><a href="https://www.instagram.com/reel/DfnBc6xKrYB/">Chicago&#x27;s first self-cleaning public toilet</a> by @se.kwon</li>
  </ul>
  </details>

### Bears Ears National Monument

#### Utah

##### Petroglyphs

- **5. [Newspaper Rock](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Newspaper Rock, Bears Ears National Monument, Monticello, Utah)** — Bears Ears National Monument, Monticello
  - **Best for:** Petroglyphs / One of the largest petroglyph panels in the US — 'I just CAN'T get over these petroglyphs!' Christian films the Newspaper Rock panel — a desert-varnish Wingate sandstone face in Indian Creek Canyon (Bears Ears) covered with 650+ carvings: human figures, deer, bighorn sheep, birds, footprints, handprints and spirals, etched over roughly 2,000 years by Archaic, Basketmaker, Fremont and Pueblo peoples. It's a short walk from the paved pullout on UT-211; you view the panel from behind a railing. 'History is so fascinating to me — I just want to learn more and more.'
  - Coordinates: Wikipedia (Newspaper Rock State Historic Monument); visitutah's published GPS (37.988325, -109.518501) agrees. The reel's tagged location points at Bears Ears National Monument generally; the panel itself is the state historic monument on UT-211, 28 mi NW of Monticello.

### Coronado National Forest

#### Arizona

##### Scenic drive

- **60. [Mount Lemmon (Catalina Highway)](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Mount+Lemmon+(Catalina+Highway)+Coronado+National+Forest+AZ)** — Coronado National Forest, Tucson
  - **Best for:** Scenic drive / 27 miles from desert saguaros to snowy alpine pines — Kelley & Carl call the Catalina Highway up Mount Lemmon one of the most dramatic drives in the country: 27 paved miles climbing over 6,000 feet from Sonoran Desert saguaro forest through oak woodland to alpine pine at Summerhaven — home to one of the southernmost ski areas in the US. Their favorite overlook is Windy Point Vista; this pin sits there.
  - Pin point is Windy Point Vista, the reel's favorite overlook on the drive (USGS GNIS via TopoQuest: 32.36813, -110.71620; the USFS Windy Point record agrees). The Mount Lemmon summit (9,157 ft) is at 32.44296, -110.78848.
  <details><summary>🎬 Sources</summary>

### Glen Canyon National Recreation Area

#### Arizona

##### Lake

- **69. [Lake Powell](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Lake Powell, Glen Canyon National Recreation Area, Page, Arizona)** — Glen Canyon National Recreation Area, Page
  - **Best for:** Lake / Boating, jet skiing and kayaking from Antelope Point Marina — Their complete Lake Powell guide — 'easily the most enjoyable thing we did in all of Arizona': rent a boat, jet ski or kayak, or split a houseboat with a group. They rented their jet ski from Antelope Point Marina. You can also kayak to Antelope Canyon from Antelope Point (about 3.5 miles one way) for a crowd-free stretch of the canyon. Car-reachable sunset viewpoints are the Navajo Mountain Viewpoint and Wahweap Viewpoint; Alstrom Point is the 4x4-only option. Glen Canyon NRA entry is $30 per vehicle or free with an America the Beautiful Pass; no drones. Start early for the calmest water.
  - Coordinates: Antelope Point Marina's published GPS (Forever Resorts) — the marina where Kelley & Carl rented their jet ski.

### Havasu Canyon (Havasupai)

#### Arizona

##### Waterfall

- **100. [Havasu Falls](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Havasu+Falls+AZ)** — Havasu Canyon (Havasupai), Supai
  - **Best for:** Waterfall — Justine calls the Havasupai hike '1000% YES — the best experience of my life': the hike in, the waterfalls, and the unreal turquoise water (her toes, she admits, tell a different story). The reel asks whether the $455 permit was worth it and lets the view answer — Havasu Falls pouring over the red rock into its turquoise pool.
  - 🥾 AllTrails: [Trail page](https://www.alltrails.com/trail/us/arizona/havasu-falls-mooney-falls-and-beaver-falls)
  - Access is by Havasupai Tribe reservation/permit only. Coordinates verified against OpenStreetMap.

- **101. [Mooney Falls](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Mooney+Falls+Havasupai+AZ)** — Havasu Canyon (Havasupai), Supai
  - **Best for:** Waterfall / Nearly 200-foot falls reached by a chain-and-ladder cliff descent — Episode 5 of Cassie Compton's (@lafftravel) 'hikes to do before your knees give out': Mooney Falls drops nearly 200 feet into the most ridiculously blue water she's ever seen — but reaching the base means climbing down a cliff on chains, ladders and footholds carved into the rock. It's part of the Havasupai backpacking trip (10 miles in with a 35-pound pack on her first-ever backpacking trip; she lost three toenails and would do it all again in a heartbeat). A Havasupai reservation and permit are required, and the descent is steep and slippery — definitely not for everyone, but unforgettable if you're comfortable with heights.
  - 🥾 AllTrails: [Trail page](https://www.alltrails.com/trail/us/arizona/mooney-falls-from-supai)
  - Coordinates are OpenStreetMap's Mooney Falls waterfall point on Havasu Creek, about a mile below Havasu Falls.

### Hell Hole Canyon

#### Utah

##### Waterfall

- **102. [Kayenta Falls](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Kayenta+Falls+Ivins+UT)** — Hell Hole Canyon, Ivins
  - **Best for:** Waterfall — One of Southern Utah's rarest sights, per Mikey Loveridge: the 1,000-foot red-rock cliffs of Hell Hole Canyon near Ivins run bone dry most days, but after heavy rain three ephemeral waterfalls — Kayenta Falls — pour straight down the cliff faces in a vertical flash flood. He photographed the canyon completely dry on Nov 1, 2026, and in full flow the next day after the rain kept coming.
  - 🥾 AllTrails: [Trail page](https://www.alltrails.com/trail/us/utah/hellhole-trail)
  - Pin is approximate: the ephemeral falls are not a mapped feature, so it sits on Kayenta Wash at the mouth of Hell Hole Canyon, just northwest of the Kayenta community in Ivins (OpenStreetMap). The falls flow only after heavy rain.

### Highway 128 — Colorado River Scenic Byway

#### Utah

##### Scenic drive

- **103. [Highway 128 (Upper Colorado River Scenic Byway)](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Highway+128+Moab+UT)** — Highway 128 — Colorado River Scenic Byway, Moab
  - **Best for:** Scenic drive — Nate's bucket-list drive: Utah's Highway 128, the Upper Colorado River Scenic Byway out of Moab — the road runs right along the Colorado River between towering orange cliffs. His timing tip from the caption: start about an hour and a half before official sunset.

### Red Hollow Slot Canyon

#### Utah

##### Slot canyon

- **126. [Red Slot Canyon (Red Hollow)](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Red+Hollow+Slot+Canyon+Orderville+UT)** — Red Hollow Slot Canyon, Orderville
  - **Best for:** Slot canyon — Giselle's Zion alternative #2: a 1.2-mile round-trip slot canyon with glowing orange and pink walls. Park at the water facility at the end of Red Hollow Drive — and note the sandy road is popular with off-roaders, so it can be soft going.

### Toquerville Falls (La Verkin Creek)

#### Utah

##### Waterfall

- **144. [Toquerville Falls](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Toquerville+Falls+UT)** — Toquerville Falls (La Verkin Creek), Toquerville
  - **Best for:** Waterfall — Giselle's Zion alternative #3: no hiking required if you have a 4x4 (don't attempt it in a normal car) — a 5.3-mile dirt road, about 45 minutes, to falls that pour over two pour-offs on La Verkin Creek: a cascade section and a clean 20-foot drop into a pool. ### Dinosaur National Monument

#### Utah

##### Fossils · A building built around a wall of dinosaur bones

- **10. [Quarry Exhibit Hall](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Quarry+Exhibit+Hall+Dinosaur+National+Monument)** — Dinosaur National Monument, Jensen
  - **Best for:** Fossils · A building built around a wall of dinosaur bones — About 30 minutes east of Vernal, a shuttle takes you to the Quarry Exhibit Hall — a building constructed around the sloped rock face where a 'log jam' of dinosaur bones was found in 1909. Hundreds of thousands of bones were excavated for museums around the world, but the rest were left in place, so you can see — and touch — real fossils where they were buried. You can shuttle back or hike back down for more fossils in the rock formations. The monument spans Utah and Colorado; the quarry is on the Utah side, and the creators wished they'd had time for more trails and a Green River float.
  <details><summary>🎬 Sources</summary>
  <ul>
  <li><a href="https://www.instagram.com/reel/DdglrAsBsTg/">Finding, seeing, touching dinosaur fossils at Dinosaur National Monument</a> by @the_vg_odyssey</li>
  </ul>
  </details>

### East Zion (Orderville)

#### Utah

##### Slot canyon

- **11. [Crimson Canyon](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Crimson+Canyon+East+Zion+Adventures+Orderville)** — East Zion (Orderville), Orderville
  - **Best for:** Slot canyon / Guided tour · Antelope-style canyon without the crowds — The reel's pitch: people pay hundreds to visit Antelope Canyon, but almost no one knows about this slot canyon near Zion — towering red sandstone walls (100+ ft high, 6–10 ft wide), winding passageways and incredible photo opportunities WITHOUT the crowds. The catch, stated honestly in the reel: Crimson Canyon itself has no entrance fee, but you can't access it independently because the route crosses private property — you book a guided tour with a company that has permission. They booked East Zion Adventures and loved it: a ~2-hour trip, UTV ride into the backcountry from Orderville, then a guided hike with short climbs (obstacles up to ~10 ft).
  - Pin is the tour meeting point in Orderville (15 E State St — check-in at the Sinclair station coffee shop, per East Zion Adventures' listings); the canyon itself is on private land reached by UTV and has no public coordinates.
  <details><summary>🎬 Sources</summary>

  - **Best for:** Hike / Many Glacier trail past turquoise lakes to a shrinking glacier — Rated 10/10 in Kelley & Carl's honest ratings for Montana & Wyoming hikes — one of the finest trails in Glacier National Park, climbing past Grinnell Lake's impossible turquoise water to the glacier itself. - **16. [Highline Trail](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Highline+Trail+Glacier+National+Park+MT)** — Glacier National Park, West Glacier
  - **Best for:** Hike / Glacier's signature cliff-edge traverse along the Garden Wall — Rated 9/10 in Kelley & Carl's honest ratings for Montana & Wyoming hikes: the Highline Trail traverses the Garden Wall from Logan Pass — wildflowers, cliff-edge ledges with a cable handhold, and constant views.   - **Best for:** Hike / Summit view — Caption names the Mt Henry Trail in Glacier National Park.   - **Best for:** Hike — Renata's Glacier hike: a 5 AM start from Lake McDonald, a foggy forest climb she calls boring — until the stone Sperry Chalet appears on its cliff, a mountain goat poses nearby, and the scenery turns 'INSANE': ice formations, snowfields by a glacier, and her jaw on the floor. Dinner afterwards at the Lake McDonald lodge.

  - **Best for:** Hike — Ranked #5, an 8-mile round trip with about 4,500 feet of gain, mostly off-trail on the second half. He stopped short of the summit in snow but had views of Lake McDonald.

- **20. [The Garden Wall](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=The+Garden+Wall+Glacier+National+Park+MT)** — Glacier National Park, West Glacier
  - **Best for:** Hike / The Continental Divide arête above the Highline Trail, up to Grinnell Glacier Overlook — On Kelley & Carl's most-rewarding-hikes list: the Garden Wall section of the Highline Trail. Their hardest-hikes list gives the full route — 15.2 miles with over 3,400 ft of gain, the best viewpoint requiring a ~1,000 ft climb in 1 mile from the Highline up to the Grinnell Glacier Overlook. Rated 10/10 in their Montana & Wyoming ratings.
  - Pin is the published Wikipedia coordinate for the Garden Wall arête along the Continental Divide north of Logan Pass.

  - **Best for:** Hike / Giant trees · Old-growth cedar and hemlock loop at Avalanche Creek — Ranked #1 of the carousel's 10 hikes among giant trees: walk beneath western redcedars and hemlocks near Avalanche Creek in Glacier National Park, Montana. The accessible boardwalk loop also passes Avalanche Gorge, where the creek squeezes through polished rock.

  - **Best for:** Hiking / Milky-turquoise lake in the Many Glacier valley — One of Kelley & Carl's favorite Glacier hikes: Cracker Lake, a long day hike from Many Glacier to an impossibly milky-turquoise lake backed by Mount Siyeh and the Cracker Lake headwall, past an old mine site.

### Homestead Resort

#### Utah

##### Hot spring · Swim inside a 55-foot limestone crater

- **48. [Homestead Crater](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Homestead+Crater+Midway+UT)** — Homestead Resort, Midway
  - **Best for:** Hot spring · Swim inside a 55-foot limestone crater — A hidden underground hot spring inside a 55-foot-tall limestone crater: a naturally heated geothermal pool at 90–96°F year-round, about 65 feet deep, that you can soak, swim, snorkel or even scuba dive in. It's at the Homestead Resort in Midway, just outside Park City, but day visitors are welcome — $30 per person (the reel notes it was $15 when filmed) for a 60-minute session with about 40 minutes in the water; life jackets are required and provided, and reservations are recommended since weekends fill up.

### Million Dollar Highway (Ouray to Silverton)

#### Colorado

##### Scenic drive

- **57. [Million Dollar Highway (US-550)](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Million+Dollar+Highway+Colorado)** — Million Dollar Highway (Ouray to Silverton), Ouray
  - **Best for:** Scenic drive — American Travel Archives' 'you will NOT believe this road' drive: the Million Dollar Highway (US-550) from Ouray to Silverton — 25 miles through the San Juan Mountains famous for steep cliffs, tight switchbacks and few guardrails. Stop at Red Mountain Pass for the classic overlook; autumn is the best time, when golden aspens contrast with the red and gray rock. Their tips: drive it in good morning light, take your time at the pull-offs, and think twice in an RV. Ouray and Silverton bookend it with hot springs and silver-mining history.
  - Pin is at Red Mountain Pass, the highway's classic overlook (OpenStreetMap).

### Royal Gorge, Cañon City depot

#### Colorado

##### Scenic train

- **67. [Royal Gorge Route Railroad](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Royal+Gorge+Route+Railroad+Canon+City)** — Royal Gorge, Cañon City depot, Cañon City
  - **Best for:** Scenic train / Canyon views · 1,000-ft gorge from an open-air car — Insane canyon views without hiking or driving sketchy roads: the Royal Gorge Route Railroad out of Cañon City, Colorado (~1 hr from Colorado Springs). The train runs the Arkansas River through a 1,000+ ft deep canyon with sheer granite cliffs on both sides, passing under the famous Royal Gorge Bridge — bald eagles, rafters, and dramatic rock formations along the route, with the best photo ops from the open-air car. Know before you go, per the reel: the ride is about 2 hours roundtrip and slow by design (scenery, not speed); parking is easy near the depot; there's a full kitchen and bar on most departures; and you can pair it with Royal Gorge Bridge Park if you have extra time.
  - Pin is the OSM station point for the Royal Gorge Route Railroad depot in Cañon City, where the ride boards.
  <details><summary>🎬 Sources</summary>

### Castle Crags Wilderness / Mount Shasta area

#### California

##### Hike

- **7. [Heart Lake Trail (from Castle Lake)](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Heart+Lake+Trail+Castle+Lake+Mount+Shasta)** — Castle Crags Wilderness / Mount Shasta area, Mount Shasta
  - **Best for:** Hike / Viewpoint · Two Mount Shasta viewpoints on one short trail — 2 incredible viewpoints, 1 short hike: the Heart Lake Trail from Castle Lake in the Mount Shasta area of Northern California. The out-and-back is only 3 miles with about 800 ft of elevation gain — not exactly easy, per the reel, but definitely doable and totally worth it for the two insane views of Mount Shasta: Heart Lake itself and the lookout above it looking back over Castle Lake toward the mountain. Trail volunteers have rerouted and marked the path with cairns and ribbons — stick to the defined trail and download offline maps to navigate.
  - 🥾 AllTrails: [Trail page](https://www.alltrails.com/trail/us/california/heart-lake-trail-from-castle-lake)
  - Pin is Castle Lake (OSM lake point), the trailhead — Heart Lake sits above it on the trail, and the Shasta viewpoints are the payoff of the climb.

### Giant Sequoia National Monument

#### California

##### Waterfall

- **34. [Seven Teacups](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Seven+Teacups+Kern+River+California)** — Giant Sequoia National Monument, Kernville
  - **Best for:** Waterfall — A surreal chain of smooth white-granite pools on Dry Meadow Creek, each cup dropping 6 to 20 feet into the next before the water slides into the Kern River. The reel names the AllTrails route 'Seven Tea Cups Viewpoint via Dry Creek Meadow' and mentions Johnny McNally's Fairview Lodge-Restaurant, about 10 minutes away, as a nearby stop (an amenity mention, not pinned).

### Golden Gate National Recreation Area / Presidio

#### California

##### Beach

- **36. [Marshall's Beach](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Marshall's+Beach+San+Francisco)** — Golden Gate National Recreation Area / Presidio, San Francisco
  - **Best for:** Beach / Viewpoint · Golden Gate views without the crowds — San Francisco's most underrated Golden Gate view — and you'll probably have it to yourself. The family's route: park at the Langdon Court lot (free, mostly empty around 10 AM), walk toward Battery West, then take the Batteries to Bluffs Trail down to the beach (~0.5 mile, stairs involved — their 4- and 5-year-olds handled it fine), turn right toward Marshall's Beach and down a few more stairs. They stayed almost an hour without seeing another person. Safety notes from the reel: don't go at high tide — the beach becomes mostly inaccessible and dangerous, so check tides first; no restrooms or facilities; and it's a clothing-optional beach, worth knowing if you're bringing kids.
  - Pin is the OSM beach point for Marshall's Beach, below the Batteries to Bluffs Trail.

### McArthur-Burney Falls Memorial State Park

#### California

##### Waterfall · 129-ft spring-fed falls flowing year-round

- **73. [Burney Falls](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Burney+Falls+California)** — McArthur-Burney Falls Memorial State Park, Burney
  - **Best for:** Waterfall · 129-ft spring-fed falls flowing year-round — Known as the '8th Wonder of the World' (Theodore Roosevelt's phrase): Burney Falls, just outside the tiny town of Burney, California — and it's only a short walk from the parking lot. The 129-foot falls push through about 100 million gallons of water a day, and because they're mainly fed by underground springs they flow all year round. A little over an hour from Redding, which the reel suggests as home base. Note from the reel: during peak summer season, weekend visits need a reservation booked in advance (none needed after late September).
  - 🥾 AllTrails: [Trail page](https://www.alltrails.com/trail/us/california/burney-falls-loop-trail)

### Thiên Long Sơn (Dragon Mountain Park)

#### California

##### Peak

- **102. [Dragon Mountain Peak](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Dragon+Mountain+Park+Milpitas)** — Thiên Long Sơn (Dragon Mountain Park), Milpitas
  - **Best for:** Peak / Stairs climb · Buddhist statues and valley views from a temple hill — One of 9 hikes on Tenzin Bhutti's 'Bay Area hikes you don't want to miss' list (waterfalls, coastal trails, beautiful views). Dragon Mountain in Milpitas — the Thiên Long Sơn temple park: a 450+ step staircase climb past Buddhist statues to a grassy summit with views across Silicon Valley to Loma Prieta and Mount Umunhum. The out-and-back runs about 4 miles from the lower lot at 3215 Calaveras Rd; open sunrise to sunset, no dogs.
  - Pin is the OSM point for Dragon Mountain Park (the temple grounds); the summit boulders are above it on the trail.

### Alpine Lakes Wilderness

#### Washington

##### Hike

- **1. [Snow Lake (Alpine Lakes)](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Snow+Lake+Trail+Snoqualmie+Pass+WA)** — Alpine Lakes Wilderness, Snoqualmie Pass
  - **Best for:** Hike — The Trekking Mama's 'how is this real?' lake: Snow Lake looks like it should require a plane ticket or a major expedition, but the trailhead is only about 60 minutes from Seattle. The water is an unbelievable bright alpine blue that looks photoshopped but isn't. It's popular and you'll share the trail — her tip is to keep going past the first viewpoints down toward the end of the lake, where the crowds thin out. Her go-to when someone visits Washington and needs a massive dose of alpine gorgeousness without planning a whole trip.
  - 🥾 AllTrails: [Trail page](https://www.alltrails.com/trail/us/washington/snow-lake-trail)
  - The Alpine Lakes Wilderness Snow Lake near Snoqualmie Pass — a different lake from the Snow Lake in Mount Rainier National Park, which is a separate pin. Pin is OpenStreetMap's named point for the lake.

##### Hiking

  - **Best for:** Hiking / Permit-only alpine basin of turquoise lakes and granite peaks — The Enchantments near Leavenworth top Kelley & Carl's list of places for nature lovers that aren't national parks — a turquoise alpine-lake basin in the Alpine Lakes Wilderness (their lakes list approaches it via the 9-mile Colchuck Lake hike).
  - Pin at the Stuart Lake Trailhead, the main Enchantments entrance; coordinates from the USFS trailhead record.

### Alvord Desert

#### Oregon

##### Stargazing

- **3. [Alvord Desert](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Alvord+Desert+Oregon)** — Alvord Desert, Fields
  - **Best for:** Stargazing — Jess drove 9 hours to camp on the Alvord Desert playa — under some of the darkest skies in Oregon — to teach herself astrophotography. She timed the trip under an almost-full moon by accident, so she waited for moonset, set a 3:24 AM alarm, and manually shot 105 long exposures (her old Sony has no intervalometer) to stitch a four-second starlapse. Her verdict: the Alvord had been on her list a long time and was worth every bit of the drive.
  - Coordinates verified against OpenStreetMap.

### Cascade Head Scenic Research Area

#### Oregon

##### Hike

- **7. [God's Thumb (The Thumb via the Knoll)](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=God's Thumb (The Thumb via the Knoll), Cascade Head Scenic Research Area, Lincoln City, Oregon)** — Cascade Head Scenic Research Area, Lincoln City
  - **Best for:** Hike / Coastal headland viewpoint over the Pacific — Emily's hike info for The Thumb via the Knoll Trail in Lincoln City: 4 miles with 987 ft of elevation gain — you'll gain 600 ft in the first mile, 'like climbing a staircase to heaven,' but the steep incline is worth it when you reach the top and see how The Thumb (a grass-topped basalt headland over the Pacific) gets its name. The route passes The Knoll meadow viewpoint on Lincoln City open space before the user-made path out to the Thumb. Practical notes from her caption: dog friendly, no restrooms, street parking that can get backed up — and IMPORTANT: do not take the trail at the end of the cul-de-sac; the trail begins on the left side.
  - Coordinates: Mapcarta / OpenStreetMap natural=peak point for God's Thumb; Explorest's published trail-end viewpoint (45.0281, -124.0082) agrees. Trailhead is the Villages at Cascade Head / Knoll trailhead at the end of NE Devils Lake Blvd.

### Green River Gorge

#### Washington

##### Waterfall

- **16. [Green River Gorge Resort](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Green+River+Gorge+Resort+Enumclaw)** — Green River Gorge, Enumclaw
  - **Best for:** Waterfall / Hidden gem · Walk behind a waterfall into a cave — Don't miss this hidden gem: the Green River Gorge Resort property near Enumclaw, WA. The resort dates to the 1920s, when it operated as a privately owned getaway with a hotel and cabins; by the 1970s and '80s it had become a well-known local party spot. The resort itself no longer operates, but the property and trails are still accessible — check out the bridge, walk behind a waterfall into a hidden cave, and explore the area's unique rock formations. The reel's practical notes: $5 for parking, paid at a cash box; no restrooms; and the trail can be slippery, so watch your step. Leave no trace.
  - Pin is the published Green River Gorge Resort point (29500 SE Green River Gorge Rd, Enumclaw) — the trail access for the gorge, bridge, and waterfall cave.
  <details><summary>🎬 Sources</summary>

  </ul>
  </details>

### Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Mountain Loop Highway)

#### Washington

##### Summit hike

- **17. [Vesper Peak](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Vesper+Peak+Trail+Washington)** — Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Mountain Loop Highway), Granite Falls
  - **Best for:** Summit hike / Sunset · Steep alpine climb to a 6,214-ft summit — Sunset on Vesper Peak — one of the most rewarding hikes off Washington's Mountain Loop Highway. The reel's card: about 6.5 miles round trip with 4,120 ft of gain; plan 6–8 hours (their hike took 5h40, and it runs longer than it looks — preparation is key, carry the 10 essentials). The trail starts in forest with steady switchbacks, then opens to alpine meadows, rocky slopes and big views; Vesper Lake near the top is a beautiful break spot (filter any water); the last stretch is steep and rocky. Sunset tip: start early enough to be at the summit before golden hour and bring a headlamp for the hike down. Pack layers, extra water, and traction in early season (snow can linger into summer); a Northwest Forest Pass is needed at the trailhead.
  - 🥾 AllTrails: [Trail page](https://www.alltrails.com/trail/us/washington/vesper-peak-trail)
  - Pin is the OSM summit point for Vesper Peak (6,214 ft); the hike starts at the Sunrise Mine trailhead off the Mountain Loop Highway.
  <details><summary>🎬 Sources</summary>
  <ul>
  <li><a href="https://www.instagram.com/reel/DeqN16QRkeF/">Sunset on Vesper Peak — one of the most rewarding hikes off the Mountain Loop Highway</a> by @nia.patience</li>
  </ul>
  </details>

### Mount Rainier National Park (Sunrise)

#### Washington

##### Hike

- **28. [Burroughs Mountain Trail](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Burroughs+Mountain+Trail+Mount+Rainier+National+Park+(Sunrise)+WA)** — Mount Rainier National Park (Sunrise), Ashford
  - **Best for:** Hike / Tundra ridge walk across First, Second and Third Burroughs above Sunrise — Rated a perfect 10/10 in Kelley & Carl's Washington hike ratings. Their hardest-hikes list: 9.6 miles with 2,614 ft of gain and significant sun exposure — rewarded with epic, sustained Mount Rainier views the whole way.
  - 🥾 AllTrails: [Trail page](https://www.alltrails.com/trail/us/washington/burroughs-mountain-loop-trail)
  - Pin is the OSM Third Burroughs Mountain summit point — the far end of the Burroughs ridge trail from Sunrise.

### Mount Si Natural Resources Conservation Area

#### Washington

##### Hike

- **30. [Mount Si](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Mount+Si+Trail+North+Bend+WA)** — Mount Si Natural Resources Conservation Area, North Bend
  - **Best for:** Hike — WTA calls Mount Si the most popular hike in Washington — upwards of 100,000 hikers a year. The switchbacks start right at the trailhead; a mile and a half up you pass through Snag Flat, old-growth trees that survived fire and logging, then past a talus slope to the base of the Haystack, the true summit. 8.0 miles round trip with 3,150 ft of gain. Climbers training for Rainier haul heavy packs up here — the rule of thumb is that if you can make the top in under two hours, you're ready. A Discover Pass is required to park, and the lot fills early.
  - 🥾 AllTrails: [Trail page](https://www.alltrails.com/trail/us/washington/mount-si-trail)
  - Coordinates verified against OpenStreetMap.

### North Cascades / Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest

#### Washington

##### Viewpoint

- **31. [Washington Pass Overlook](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Washington+Pass+Overlook+North+Cascades+/+Okanogan-Wenatchee+National+Forest+WA)** — North Cascades / Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Winthrop
  - **Best for:** Viewpoint / Highway 20's highest overlook, staring at Liberty Bell Mountain — A don't-miss stop in Kelley & Carl's North Cascades mini guide: the Washington Pass Overlook on Highway 20 — at 5,477 feet the road's high point, with a short paved path to a railing view of Liberty Bell Mountain and the Early Winters spires.
  - Coordinates from the USFS Washington Pass Observation Site record.

### North Cascades National Park

#### Washington

##### Alpine lake · Three paternoster lakes reflecting Mount Triumph

- **32. [Thornton Lake](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Thornton+Lakes+North+Cascades)** — North Cascades National Park, Marblemount
  - **Best for:** Alpine lake · Three paternoster lakes reflecting Mount Triumph — One of the ten in Ted's 'top 10 hikes after visiting 62 of 63 national parks' list. Thornton Lake in North Cascades National Park — the lowest of three paternoster lakes below Mount Triumph, reflecting the peaks; the ~10-mile round trip climbs to a ridge above the lakes (backcountry permit to camp).
  - Coordinates are the published Thornton Lakes point (Wikipedia/GeoNames); an earlier generic name lookup returned a different Snohomish County lake and was rejected.

  - **Best for:** Hike · Ridge climb to the Sahale Glacier camp — Listed at 12 miles in the reel: switchbacks up to Cascade Pass, then the steep climb along the Sahale Arm ridge through meadows — marmots and mountain goats along the way — to the Sahale Glacier camp, ringed by North Cascades peaks.

##### Hiking

- **39. [Blue Lake Trail](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Blue+Lake+Trail+North+Cascades+National+Park+WA)** — North Cascades National Park, Marblemount
  - **Best for:** Hiking / Larch-lined alpine lake at Washington Pass — One of Kelley & Carl's favorite North Cascades hikes: the Blue Lake Trail off Highway 20 near Washington Pass — about 4.6 miles round trip to a deep-blue alpine lake under the Liberty Bell group, famous for golden larches in fall.

  - **Best for:** Hiking / Sea arch carved through a headland, reached at low tide — One of Kelley & Carl's Olympic coast picks in their most-diverse-park reel: Hole-in-the-Wall, a sea arch punched through a rocky headland about 1.5 miles north of Rialto Beach — another great one at low tide, when the tide pools around it come alive.

### Silver Falls State Park

#### Oregon

##### Waterfall

- **60. [Trail of Ten Falls](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Trail+of+Ten+Falls+Silver+Falls+State+Park)** — Silver Falls State Park, Silverton
  - **Best for:** Waterfall / Hike · Ten waterfalls on one 7.7-mile loop — The best bang-for-your-buck waterfall hike: the 7.7-mile Trail of Ten Falls at Silver Falls State Park, about an hour from Portland — and you get to walk UNDER (behind) four of the falls. The reel's tips: hike the loop clockwise, parking at the South Falls lot to start; bring a credit card ($5 parking at some lots, machines on site); expect to get a little wet walking behind the falls, so bring a rain jacket in colder months; grab the park trail map or an app like AllTrails first, since one or two falls need a side trail; dogs can't hike this trail (take them on the Rim Trail instead); and start early — it's popular.
  - Pin is the Silver Falls State Park point (OSM); the loop starts at the South Falls day-use area per the reel.

### The Enchantments (Alpine Lakes Wilderness)

#### Washington

##### Hike

- **61. [Colchuck Lake](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Colchuck+Lake+WA)** — The Enchantments (Alpine Lakes Wilderness), Leavenworth
  - **Best for:** Hike — Their candidate for the most beautiful lake in the USA: Colchuck Lake in the Enchantments outside Leavenworth. It's a 9-mile out-and-back with 2,340 ft of elevation gain (moderate-hard) — and extremely popular despite the effort. Their summer tip: get there extremely early; they arrived around 5 AM and the parking lot was nearly full, with 50+ cars along the road by the time they hiked out.

## Source reels {#source-reels}

- **[5 National Park Sunrises That Blew My Mind](https://www.instagram.com/reel/De9cpsdpbBx/)** — @amorywild · 5 places · Theme: Best national park sunrises
  - What the reel recommends: A countdown of the creator's five most memorable national park sunrises, ranked 5 to 1. Every place in this reel is recommended specifically for sunrise, not general visiting.
- **[Canyon Overlook Trail — One of Zion's Best Views](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DdMWajZA_cn/)** — @adventurefamilyvlog · 1 places · Theme: Best short hike / best view in Zion
  - What the reel recommends: Recommends Canyon Overlook Trail as one of Zion's best views at the end of a 1-mile trail: biggest payoff for least effort in Zion, ~160 ft gain, 1-2 hours, just east of the Zion-Mount Carmel Tunnel, incredible at sunrise or sunset, views over Pine Creek Canyon. This place was already on the map from the @amorywild sunrise reel, so it was added as a second source on that pin instead of a duplicate pin.
- **[Canyon Overlook Trail — Epic View Without Angels Landing](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DfP7jlPPlAI/)** — @beesforbeau · 1 places · Theme: Short hike with an epic view, Angels Landing alternative
  - What the reel recommends: Recommends Canyon Overlook Trail as an epic-view alternative to Angels Landing without the chains, climb or permit: about 1 mile round trip, allow about an hour, just east of the Zion-Mount Carmel Tunnel, with sandstone formations, rock alcoves and exposed sections. Parking is very limited, arrive early. Already on the map from two earlier reels, so added as a third source on that pin.
- **[Hiking — Four Mile Trail to Glacier Point](https://www.instagram.com/p/DGx5pUQpGri/)** — @amorywild · 1 places · Theme: Hiking
  - What the reel recommends: Caption names the Four Mile Trail to Glacier Point in Yosemite as the post's hike. No media narrative was stored for this post, so this is based on the caption only.
- **[Favorite spot in the Everglades](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DfProEQAaZY/)** — @amorywild · 1 places · Theme: Favorite spot in the Everglades
  - What the reel recommends: The reel recommends Shark Valley as a can't-miss Everglades destination about 15 miles from Miami, with a 15-mile loop road best explored by bike or on foot, wildlife including alligators and wading birds, and a spiral observation tower over the sawgrass prairie.
- **[Hiking — South Kaibab Trail](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DfNNQJJR2SI/)** — @amorywild · 1 places · Theme: Hiking
  - What the reel recommends: Caption names South Kaibab in the Grand Canyon, and on-screen text calls it one of the greatest hikes on earth. The footage shows canyon cliffs, the river below and a suspension bridge from an elevated overlook.
- **[Sunset — Badlands National Park](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DfLCfQtO7rm/)** — @amorywild · 1 places · Theme: Sunset
  - What the reel recommends: Tagged and captioned as Badlands at sunset. The video is a first-person panorama over eroded cliffs, buttes and prairie valleys as the sky turns orange, pink and yellow.
- **[5 National Park Views That Blew My Mind](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DfIBY_LB8RS/)** — @amorywild · 4 places · Theme: 5 National Park Views That Blew My Mind
  - What the reel recommends: Ranked #5 for views, shown with its summit marker and sweeping desert mountain vistas. Ranked #4 for views, with dramatic green cliffs overlooking turquoise water at Potato Harbor on Santa Cruz Island. Ranked #3 for views, showing a vast field of purple lupine flowers against forested hills. Ranked #2 for views, showing the stone staircase up Moro Rock and expansive views over layered mountain ranges. Ranked #1 for views, highlighted by the clear lake reflecting the snow-capped Teton peaks.
- **[5 National Park Hikes That Tested My Limit](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DfF8sFUPES5/)** — @amorywild · 4 places · Theme: 5 National Park Hikes That Tested My Limit
  - What the reel recommends: Ranked #5, an 8-mile round trip with about 4,500 feet of gain, mostly off-trail on the second half. He stopped short of the summit in snow but had views of Lake McDonald. Ranked #4, a 10.5-mile round trip wading the Virgin River in cold water. He went in June during snowmelt and used a dry bib wetsuit. Ranked #3, described as logistically easy but hard because of high, cold water crossings that left him constantly off-balance, wearing wetsuit overalls and layers. Ranked #2, a 17-mile route with about 4,500 feet of gain done in June with snow at the top, which he calls one of the most beautiful hikes he has done despite loose rock. Ranked #1, an 8-mile hike with about 4,500 feet of gain and turquoise lake views. He says he was unprepared on his first attempt and later returned better prepared.
- **[5 National Parks for Deafening Silence (solitude)](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DfDGoIcv13_/)** — @amorywild · 6 places · Theme: 5 National Parks for Deafening Silence (solitude)
  - What the reel recommends: Ranked #5 for solitude, with red rock and slot canyons and overlooks where he notes you might not see another person on longer trails.   - What the reel recommends: Her personal Lake Superior winter bucket list — three things she plans every year: (1) sunrise at Artist Point in Grand Marais, Minnesota, over the frozen lake at 20 below zero or colder; (2) the Apostle Islands ice caves — kayak the mainland sea caves in summer, or walk across the frozen lake when the Park Service opens foot access; (3) Michigan's Keweenaw Peninsula for skiing, frozen waterfalls and sauna. All three are new pins (places identified from the reel's narration; the caption itself names no places).
- **[57 parks down — our favorite parks, by category](https://www.instagram.com/p/DfhnyRAlb-N/)** — @katieandjoeonthego · 23 places · Theme: Favorite national parks by category (57 parks visited)
  - What the reel recommends: Katie & Joe — 57 of the 64 US national parks visited, 7 left — award 23 parks their own titles instead of picking one favorite: Mount Rainier (hiking), Capitol Reef (snacks), Carlsbad Caverns (otherworldly vibes), Olympic (camping), White Sands (sunsets), Acadia (sunrise), Bryce Canyon (stargazing), Yosemite (waterfalls), Great Smoky Mountains (fall foliage), Katmai (wildlife), Gates of the Arctic (feel small), Lake Clark (solitude), Isle Royale (backpacking), Kenai Fjords (unique experiences), Dry Tortugas (history), Death Valley (backcountry driving), Glacier (take your breath away), Wind Cave (evening program), Theodore Roosevelt (scenic drive), Gateway Arch (visitor center experience), Arches (only one day), Grand Canyon (don't want to hike), Badlands (fossils). Sources attach to the 22 existing park pins; Gateway Arch National Park is a new pin (the dataset's first for that park).
- **[Newspaper Rock petroglyphs — Bears Ears](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DflFsSEPmlS/)** — @christiandelatorre_ · 1 places · Theme: Newspaper Rock petroglyphs (Bears Ears)
  - What the reel recommends: Christian de la Torre at Newspaper Rock, Utah — panning shots of the famous petroglyph panel in Indian Creek Canyon (Bears Ears National Monument): 650+ carvings (figures, animals, footprints, handprints, spirals) spanning ~2,000 years, viewed from behind a railing at a roadside pullout on UT-211. 'I just can't get over these petroglyphs — history is so fascinating.' One new pin.
- **[Battery Spencer — best Golden Gate view](https://www.instagram.com/reel/Dec472wPcYx/)** — @thisworldofadventure · 1 places · Theme: Battery Spencer / Golden Gate Bridge viewpoint
  - What the reel recommends: Courtney & Matt's bucket-list Golden Gate viewpoint: Battery Spencer, the historic gun battery high above the bridge on the Marin Headlands (Sausalito side). Quick stop, huge payoff — views of the bridge, San Francisco and the bay. Go about an hour before sunset and stay through it; the colors keep improving. Fog can roll in fast and wipe the view. One new pin.
- **[God's Thumb via the Knoll — Lincoln City](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DfkoEFpvMBW/)** — @littleredtravels · 1 places · Theme: God's Thumb / Oregon Coast hikes
  - What the reel recommends: Emily's (@littleredtravels) hike guide to God's Thumb via the Knoll Trail, Lincoln City, Oregon: 4 miles, 987 ft gain, 600 ft of it in the first mile ('a staircase to heaven'), through The Knoll meadow to the basalt headland above the Pacific. Dog friendly, no restrooms, street parking; don't take the cul-de-sac trail — the trail starts on the left. One new pin.
- **[Chicago's first self-cleaning public toilet](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DfnBc6xKrYB/)** — @se.kwon · 1 places · Theme: Chicago first — self-cleaning public toilet at the Polish Triangle
  - What the reel recommends: A tour of Chicago's first self-cleaning public toilet — the new JCDecaux automated restroom at the Polish Triangle in Wicker Park/West Town, opened Nov 11, 2026: free, ADA-compliant, 15-minute limit, and the bowl self-disinfects with high-pressure jets between uses.
- **[Part 2 of Free 10/10 Viewpoints in San Francisco](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DcedEqhyDgs/)** — @dhillon.diary · 4 places · Theme: Free 10/10 viewpoints in San Francisco — Part 2
  - What the reel recommends: Part 2 of her free 10/10 San Francisco viewpoints, in order: Pier 7 at dusk, Crissy Field Beach at golden hour, Alta Plaza Park, and the Lands End hike — all free, all for friends or a solo clear-your-mind visit.
- **[Grosse Point Lighthouse | Evanston, Illinois](https://www.instagram.com/reel/Dfm9oLGIudt/)** — @icynthiareds · 1 places · Theme: Historic lighthouse near Chicago
  - What the reel recommends: A visual tour of the Grosse Point Lighthouse in Evanston — a historic 1873 lighthouse on the Lake Michigan shore, about 30 minutes from downtown Chicago, one of the prettiest and most historic corners of Evanston and worth adding to a Chicago-area visit list.
- **[3 BEST SPOTS FOR SUNSET IN DOOR COUNTY](https://www.instagram.com/reel/Dfm-r58AHrq/)** — @officetooutdoorsblog · 3 places · Theme: Sunset in Door County
  - What the reel recommends: Three sunset spots in Door County, Wisconsin, ranked: Ellison Bluff County Park in Ellison Bay (cliffside overlook above Green Bay), Sunset Beach Park in Fish Creek (sun straight into the bay from a rocky shore and grassy bluff), and Pebble Beach in Sister Bay (a quiet, secluded pebble shoreline).
- **[Experience one of Acadia's hidden gems!](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DfniyeIICMI/)** — @ryan.goes.hiking · 1 places · Theme: Hidden-gem hike in Acadia
  - What the reel recommends: Penobscot Mountain Trail in Acadia National Park — a hidden gem across Jordan Pond from the Bubbles hikes, 2.9 miles out-and-back with 980 feet of gain to a ~1,200-foot summit with 360-degree views of the pond, mountains and Atlantic; rated hard on AllTrails.
- **[Indiana World War Memorial, Indianapolis](https://www.instagram.com/reel/Dfm6ewDuePk/)** — @englishman_in_indiana · 2 places · Theme: Historic war memorial in Indianapolis
  - What the reel recommends: The Indiana World War Memorial in downtown Indianapolis — a 210-foot neoclassical monument of Indiana limestone modelled on the Mausoleum at Halicarnassus, with a museum and atrium inside — and the 100-foot Veterans Memorial Obelisk opposite it, rising from a pink marble fountain with four bronze sculptures for law, science, religion and education.

## How this page is updated {#how-this-page-is-updated}

Send Muse an Instagram reel link in chat. Muse reads the caption and the video itself, extracts every named location, verifies and geocodes each one, assigns its region and state, records what the reel recommended it for and a link to the reel, then regenerates this list and the map from `places.json` and pushes the update to GitHub Pages. Duplicates (same name + state) are not added twice.
